what_this_is: The Workshop rows for trading at the person's own broker: place the orders of a trading policy, check placed orders, and look up listed instruments, each once for a paper account and once for a live one. A row holds only its own mode's broker credentials and reaches only that mode's records.

payload.label: Place paper orders from a trading policy
payload.job: Place the orders of my trading policy at my broker's paper account
payload.description: Give policy (its version, its orders, and its own limits: risk.max_order_notional, risk.max_daily_notional and risk.day_time_zone; risk.allowed_symbols, when given, is the only symbols it may trade), routes (how your broker takes an order, each route with mode "paper") and prices for market orders. Every order is checked first and skipped with its reason when it is malformed, says live: true, has no paper route, was already sent for this policy version, names a symbol outside risk.allowed_symbols, or would pass a limit; nothing is resized. Give records too (the trade-order and trade-day-spend records of earlier runs, read from the store that holds them): they say what was already sent and how much of the day's limit is used. Nothing is kept here: the answer's records are the trade-order, trade-order-event and trade-day-spend records this run would write, for you to keep; a 4xx answer is a refusal, and no answer is "unknown" and is never sent again once its record is handed back. With no policy nothing is sent and the answer says what to give. The held paper-broker-credentials (a JSON object of named fields) reach only the request and are never kept or shown.

policy.description: The trading policy: { policy_version, decided_at?, orders: [{ instrument: { symbol, kind?, contract_multiplier? }, side, qty, order_type, limit_price?, time_in_force?, live: false, route_ref }], risk: { max_order_notional, max_daily_notional, day_time_zone, allowed_symbols? } }

routes.description: The person's broker routes by route_ref, each with mode "paper", instrument_requests, credential_injections, response_map and status_map (tools/trading/README.md)

prices.description: A price for each symbol a market order names: { <symbol>: <price> }

records.description: The trade-order and trade-day-spend records of earlier runs, [{ id, type, value }], as the store that holds them returned them; leave out for a first run. Only records whose id starts with paper- are read.
The trade-order, trade-order-event and trade-day-spend records this run would write, [{ id, type, value }], for you to keep.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages trade-order (decide-orders, assemble-order-request, parse-broker-order, merge-headers) and trade-audit (the order trail), ported Keeps nothing: earlier trade-order and trade-day-spend records come in the request as records and the records a run would write come back in the answer (w7-tools-keep-nothing).

payload.label: Check paper orders with the broker
payload.job: Check my paper orders with my broker: which are filled, at what price, and which never got there
payload.description: Give routes (the same routes the orders were placed with, each with status_request and open_statuses). Give records too (the paper trade-order records to check, and the trade-day-spend records, read from the store that holds them). Every paper order still open (sending, unknown, or a status in the route's open_statuses) is asked about at the broker, and its record takes the broker's real status and fill; order_ids checks those orders whatever their status. An order the broker never named and does not know is marked not-placed and its day's spend is given back. Nothing is kept here: the answer's records are the changed trade-order and trade-day-spend records and a trade-order-event for each answer, for you to keep. The held paper-broker-credentials reach only the request.

payload.label: Look up instruments at my paper broker
payload.job: Find the instruments my broker lists for trading, such as option contracts, from my paper account
payload.description: Give route (one broker route with mode "paper" and its lookups), lookup (a lookup's name) and query (by the names the lookup allows; the lookup's own defaults fill the rest). A lookup is any read the broker answers: its listed instruments, the account (a lookup with one_item reads the one object as one item, for example equity and buying power) or the positions held. Answers the listed items the lookup keeps (for example only tradable ones), numbers read as numbers, sorted as the lookup says, with the next page token. An error answer carries no items. The held paper-broker-credentials reach only the request.

payload.label: Read my trading account board
payload.job: Show my trading account: its value, today's change and goal, its own figures and what I hold, from the trading agent's last cycle
payload.description: Give cycle: the fact the trading agent keeps as its last cycle (agent:trading-momentum.last-cycle), as the store holds it (its value_json) or the cycle object itself. It only reads what you give: nothing is kept, sent or read from a broker. It answers live (true when the cycle was given and reads), headline (value, deltaValue, deltaPct, deltaTone, goalLabel, goalProgressPct, equitySeries), account (the cycle's own scalar figures) and positions (one record per holding; an option contract carries its label, such as AAPL $150 Call · Jan 16 '26). Without a readable cycle it answers live false and says nothing about the account.

cycle.description: The trading agent's last-cycle fact as the store holds it ({ value_json }), or the cycle object itself.

provenance.source: bitfield-packages portfolio-connector read-data/account-board.ts and trade-order read-data/trade-order-live.ts (the OCC label), d926b7adb: the hero, balances, holdings and label reads, which no tool row reached until this one. Reads only: the cycle is given by the caller and nothing is kept.
